# Historical PowerPC Darwin 10 cross-toolchain integration

The OSXCross `ppc-test` branch, pinned at `af8300c6b3e099c91970a8d2d0f3bffe703f2421`, has the original PPC assembler and ld64 compatibility patch (`patches/ld64-add-ppc-support.patch`). Its build selector enables that patch only for Darwin 8 and 9, even though Snow Leopard's 10.6 SDK and PowerPC binaries require Darwin 10. Apply `patches/osxcross-ppc-test-darwin10.patch` to that exact checkout with `git apply --check` followed by `git apply`; the change enables the existing PowerPC patch and PPC wrappers for Darwin 10 when the SDK contains PPC support.

This is a compatibility input, **not** a claim of a successful cross-toolchain build. The build still requires the pinned legacy cctools/ld64 source and an authorized MacOSX10.6 SDK; test resulting objects with `tools/inspect_ppc_macho.py` and native PPC hardware before accepting any binary. The newer OSXCross mainline and cctools-port mainline do not advertise PowerPC targets. The independently inspected `Scottcjn/ppc-distcc` checkout at `2ec2e147c4b49206f5a762a595f3ca74b1aa1aaf` uses GCC/cctools for Darwin 9 and is a separate reference, not a drop-in Darwin 10 toolchain.
